Next steps after receiving redhat account activated email

Posted on 2021-04-30 | In Procedure

Due to new project needs, Red Hat help to create few corporate accounts for us. Its partner manager will forward the IT help desk email to the individual once the account activated. What to do next?

Prerequisites

  • The email which have the temporary token code
  • The laptop might access IBM network (office or IBM VPN)

The temporary token will be active for the next 5 days since the effective start date.

Procedures

Access Red Hat mail system

Redhat mail system uses Gmail services, so we need to use a proxy(e.g. proxy.emea.ibm.com:80) at first.

  • Browse to Redhat mail system
  • Sign in with the credentials you got, which have the username and temporary token code.
  • Find an email with subject “New Hire Vital Information PLEASE READ”, follow its guideline to set up permanent passwords. The following steps are same, but with the key points I have verified, just for your reference.

Configure the Red Hat VPN

Because we don’t use a laptop provided by Red Hat (tag our laptop as Non-CSB Macs, and their IT does not currently support), but we can set up an OpenVPN client following the article KB0009053.

  • Download VPN profiles from here, unzip the archive.
  • Download the latest stable version of Tunnelblick from here, and install it with option “I have configuration files”.
  • Click the Tunnelblick icon on the top menu bar, select “VPN Details…” to view the configuration window, drag “Red Hat Global VPN.ovpn” from the unzipped VPN profiles folder, choose to add the profile for all users. Repeat this step with any regional servers you want to add.
  • Click the Tunnelblick icon on the top menu bar, select a connection to connect the Red Hat VPN. You might try several times if have some errors.

Set a permanent Kerberos password

This phase can follow the article KB0000072.

  • Connect to the Red Hat VPN firstly
  • Go to RESET YOUR IPA/KERBEROS PASSWORD portal
  • Complete all the fields with your temporary token, then click “Set” button at the bottom right. If success, it will prompt up a message “SUCCESS. Both IdM and Kerberos Passwords have been reset!”

Set up a permanent Pin+Token

Red Hat use a two-part code called a PIN and Token to access the Virtual Private Network (VPN), Workday, and most sites with a URL including “corp.redhat.com.” A PIN is a secret password that you set. A Token is a randomized, one-time use code created by a token device. Because this login method requires two parts, it is also known as “two-factor authentication”(a.k.a. 2FA). EMC did the same when I worked there, here we choose soft token due to we can’t apply hard token device so far.

This phase can follow the article KB0004383.

  • Install FreeOTP app on your mobile device. iOS follows up KB0004382, Android system can download the latest apk file from F-Droid due to we can’t access Google Play Store.
  • Connect to the Red Hat VPN, go to RED HAT 2FA with your Kerberos password.
  • On the left side of the page, click Create Software Token, ensure the box for “Generate OTP Key on the Server” is checked under “Token data”.
  • Enter your PIN, click Enroll Token button, a new page will display a QR code.
  • Open the FreeOTP app on your mobile device, tap the QR code symbol to scan the displayed QR code using your camera.

Access your Red Hat email with new credentials

  • Connect to the Red Hat VPN or IBM VPN with a proxy, browse to Redhat mail system.
  • Enter your Red Hat email address and 2FA PIN+token if prompted, the soft token can be got by tapping the token on the FreeOTP app.
